text:
maya: heads up — rolling the new batch-threshold changes to prod looks like it bumped p95 on route-tier 'chat-high' to ~220ms from 160ms. noticed after kernel selector tweak earlier today. :thinking:

sam: ugh. did we change any token-budget defaults for that route?

liam: I saw a KV cache miss spike around the same time — kv_hit_rate for that tier dropped from 0.92 -> 0.78 in the window. could be eviction churn after the kernel switch?

olivia: @sam we lowered max_tokens_per_batch for the low-cost path but not for high. this rollout only touched kernel hinting; nothing intentional on budgets. still, kernel change could alter microbatch sizes and evict more from kv.

maya: posting a small profiler snapshot from the instance that saw the regression:

```
Perf summary (sample window: 60s)
- p50: 48ms, p95: 218ms, p99: 420ms
- avg microbatch size: 6.1 tokens -> 4.0 tokens (post-change)
- KV miss rate (route chat-high): 22% (was 8%)
- kernel selected: matmul_v2_prefetch
- observed context-setup time increase +12ms
```

sam: that microbatch shrink matches the p95. fewer tokens => more requests processed but batching inefficiency increases tail. I think token-budget target for the route needs to be gated by p95 SLO: reduce aggressive kernel-prefetching when p95 rises.

liam: quick check: can we revert kernel selector for one canary host? runbook suggests: `PUT /runtime/canary/kernel?host=canary-12&kernel=matmul_v1`. want to isolate.

perf-bot: metric snapshot uploaded: https://perf.internal/snapshots/5101234567 — alert: p95_alert(chat-high) triggered at 5101234578 :eyes: 

olivia: proposed immediate mitigation: throttle route-tier token budget down for 'chat-high' for 5m to force larger microbatches (increase tokens-per-batch target) and pin kernel back for canary. patch suggestion: `batcher.max_tokens["chat-high"] = min( default, target*1.5 )` and add SLO-gate: if p95 > 180ms then prefer conservative kernel.

maya: sounds good. @sam can you own the canary kernel revert + batcher token-gate? I’ll roll the budget tweak as a short-lived flag.

sam: on it. will revert kernel on canary-12 now and push a traffic-split to 95% -> baseline. will also add a short-circuit SLO-gate in the batcher config. ETA 20m. :thumbsup: 

liam: I’ll watch KV churn metrics and heap growth during the canary. if evictions stop, we know kernel change caused different cache access patterns.

maya: thanks — if the canary restores p95 we ship a small rollback+SLO-gate and follow up with a deeper profiling run to tune token-budget heuristics by route size and seq-dist.

perf-bot: action logged: incident-5101234567 created (priority: medium) — assign to eng-runtime.

olivia: quick note for postmortem: add a regression test that simulates kernel-induced microbatch shifts + KV cache churn. we should catch this in staging next time.

maya: agreed. closing loop after canary.
